title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump's Bid to Move Hush Money Case to Federal Court
excerpt: Judge Hellerstein rules that paying hush money is not covered by presidential immunity, keeping Trump's 34 felony convictions in New York state court.
body:
• Federal Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein denied President Trump's renewed bid to move his hush money case from New York state court to federal court, calling his arguments "neither new nor legally sufficient."
  • Hellerstein ruled that paying hush money to an adult film star is "not subsumed in presidential immunity," rejecting claims that testimony from White House aides made the case a federal matter.
  • Trump's lawyer Robert Giuffra Jr. promptly appealed the ruling to the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, keeping the legal battle alive.
  • The ruling ensures Trump's appeal of his 34 felony convictions will remain in the New York state court system, where he also has a separate appeal pending.

A federal judge on Thursday blocked President Donald Trump's renewed attempt to move his New York hush money case to federal court, dealing a fresh setback to his long-running effort to erase his criminal conviction.

U.S. District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein, in a sharply worded Aug. 28 order, said Trump "cannot play one court against another" and cannot "seek victory in one court, and then, when it becomes apparent that the court will rule against him, seek to remove his case to another court."

Judge Rejects Presidential Immunity Claims

At the center of the dispute is whether Trump's 2024 hush money conviction involved presidential conduct shielded by immunity. Trump's legal team argued that key trial evidence — including testimony from former White House communications director Hope Hicks and his former lawyer Michael Cohen — was tied to his official role as president. They contended that the Supreme Court's July 2024 ruling granting presidents broad immunity from prosecution for official acts should invalidate the conviction.

Hellerstein, who was appointed to the federal bench by President Bill Clinton, disagreed.

"Paying hush money to an adult film star or engaging in a cover-up of an embarrassment are not subsumed in presidential immunity."

— Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein, U.S. District Court

The judge called Trump's motion a "second bite at the apple," which the law "disfavors," and noted that Trump's own legal filings acknowledged the second removal attempt was filed "after the state court had all but rejected the immunity defense."

A Conviction That Keeps Haunting the Presidency

Trump was convicted in May 2024 on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in a case brought by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg. Prosecutors alleged that during the 2016 presidential campaign, Trump directed Cohen to pay $130,000 to adult film actress Stormy Daniels to buy her silence about an alleged sexual encounter, and later disguised the reimbursements as legal expenses. Trump has denied the encounter.

At his January 2025 sentencing, days before returning to office for his second term, Judge Juan Merchan imposed an unconditional discharge — no jail time, fines, or probation — saying the punishment would avoid disrupting the incoming presidency while leaving the conviction on the books.

What Comes Next

Trump's personal lawyer, Robert Giuffra Jr., promptly appealed Hellerstein's ruling to the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, according to USA Today. It was that same appeals court that had directed Hellerstein to take a second look at the case after finding his September 2024 ruling had failed to adequately consider how the Supreme Court's immunity decision affected the evidence used at trial.

The ruling means Trump's challenge to the conviction will remain in the New York state court system rather than moving to federal court, where his team hoped the immunity argument would carry more weight. Trump has also separately asked a New York state appeals court to void the conviction outright.

Of the four criminal cases Trump has faced, the Manhattan hush money prosecution brought by Bragg remains the only one that went to trial. Trump has pleaded not guilty and denied wrongdoing in all four cases.
